A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Abstract Gradient Training framework and retain matching methods, datasets, and analyses despite the changed title and focus. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection, including all appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 reports original experiments on Blobs, AMEX default prediction, OCT-MNIST, and GPT-2-based IMDb sentiment classification.

after.justification: v2 Section 4 and Appendices C and F report original certification, private-prediction, computational-budget, and unlearning results.

M1.justification: The AGT interval-training backbone remains, but v2 adds procedures converting certificates across k values into prediction-specific sensitivity bounds, Cauchy/Laplace noise calibration, and tighter privacy accounting. These substantially extend inference beyond v1's safe-prediction certification. The optional DP-SGD noise update in v1 Algorithm 1 is also omitted from v2's algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate separable and overlapping Gaussian Blobs, AMEX default prediction, OCT-MNIST normal/abnormal classification with Drusen fine-tuning, and IMDb sentiment classification using GPT-2 embeddings. AMEX moves to Appendix F.1; it is not removed. The new privacy evaluations retain these dataset/task combinations.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 5 introduces explicit smooth-sensitivity versus global-sensitivity noise-calibration comparisons on Blobs, OCT-MNIST, and IMDb. Section 4.3 also reports an AGT-versus-standard-training runtime comparison. v1 primarily compares nominal and certified behavior under training configurations, without these private-prediction baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: New prediction-noise evaluations sweep epsilon, with delta = 10^-5 for the accounting plots. OCT-MNIST's batch size changes from 3000 to 5000 and its Drusen batch proportion from 30% to 50%. Table 1 revises learning rates and decay factors for OCT-MNIST and IMDb, and reduces IMDb training from 125 to 50 epochs. Clipping values and plotted k ranges also change.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused study of the number of k values used for sensitivity estimation (Appendix C, Figure 7) and examines heterogeneous privacy-budget improvements through OCT-MNIST histograms (Figure 3). Existing depth, clipping, and training-duration analyses largely remain, while v1's Blobs comparison across two DP-SGD parameter settings is omitted.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 introduces shaded bands around noisy-accuracy curves, but their statistical meaning and computation are unspecified. Neither version identifies seeds or statistical replicate counts. v1's shaded accuracy bounds represent certification bounds, so they cannot establish an unchanged uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds privacy-utility curves, tightened-epsilon distributions, and computational-budget results. Existing certification and accuracy results also change: OCT-MNIST accuracy at gamma = 1 is 0.760 in v1 Figure 3 and 0.82 in v2 Figure 2, under revised training settings rather than a controlled performance comparison. The 125-epoch IMDb results are replaced by 50-epoch curves; AMEX's depth/batch-size findings remain.

T1.justification: v2 introduces prediction-level DP and local-sensitivity definitions, smooth-sensitivity and tighter-accounting theorems, and the Lambert-W derivation in Appendix D.1. Lemma 1 generalizes equality certification to sensitivity bounds, and Theorem 3.4 formalizes descent bounds with separate addition/removal counts. v1's membership-inference robustness theorem and proof are removed; unlearning definitions are retained and expanded in Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift the central contribution from perfect local privacy/unlearning certificates and membership-inference robustness to computable sensitivity bounds for private prediction. v2 adds claims of order-of-magnitude noise/accounting improvements and improved prediction accuracy. Unlearning becomes a secondary application, although the conclusion largely retains v1's wording.

C2.justification: v2 develops interpretations concerning sensitivity-based noise reduction, heterogeneous privacy budgets, and computational cost versus bound tightness. It explicitly distinguishes pure-DP global-sensitivity guarantees from approximate-DP accounting improvements. v1's discussions of owner-only certificate disclosure, vulnerable-record auditing, and handling noisy parameters outside certified intervals are removed. Depth-related scalability limitations remain in the relocated AMEX study.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents coordinatewise gradient truncation, revises Table 1 hyperparameters, and adds measured runtime information, including approximately 55 seconds for AGT versus 25 seconds for ordinary IMDb classifier training. Both PDFs give the same repository URL and server hardware. The clipping explanation is new disclosure; v1 does not establish a different clipping implementation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work within private prediction, adding discussion and citations concerning Dwork and Feldman, PATE, Bassily and colleagues, Nandi and Bassily, and van der Maaten and Hannun. Memorization and private-learning literature also expands, while several stewardship and attack-related references disappear. This exceeds merely moving related work to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the methodology narrative is reorganized around sensitivity and private prediction. Related work, AMEX, and much unlearning material move into reorganized appendices. The author list changes, while substantial portions of the AGT proof and conclusion remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The body changes from single-column to two-column layout, and Algorithm 1 is redrawn. Blobs, OCT-MNIST, and IMDb figure assemblies are substantially replaced or split between the main text and appendices. New sensitivity maps, privacy-budget histograms, comparative utility panels, and sensitivity-analysis figures are added. The AMEX chart is relocated with essentially unchanged content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful baseline comparisons, practical noise-calibration procedures, and a computational-budget study. However, its new Theorem 3.2 has a correctness problem as stated: for adjacent datasets producing opposite binary labels, k* = 1, epsilon = 100, and delta = 10^-5, it gives epsilonS approximately 25.26. Even after Equation 2's thresholding, one output has probability approximately 1 on one dataset, while the claimed DP inequality bounds it by approximately 10^-5 using the other dataset. This central theoretical problem competes with the empirical and explanatory gains, preventing a reliable net improvement judgment.
